prompt:
Extract data from the supplied image(s) and return a single JSON object, using the exact field names below as keys.
Below are additional instructions for specific fields  follow them exactly. Provide a value for every field; use an empty string when a value cannot be determined from the image, and do not invent data.

- The catalog number field is the unique identifier for the specimen. The format is an alpha prefix, followed but 3-8 numbers, and sometimes followed by a period and another number. It is typically found next to any barcode objects on the image. Once you have the catalog number split that value across two extra fields - the herb code [PL] and the Acc. No. using the following logic:
- The HERB code [PL] field is the prefix of the unique catalog number, either CANB or CBG or CNS or QRS
- The Acc. No field is the number part of the catalog number, it comes after the HERB code prefix. Remove any trailing period and numbers that come after the period

- Primary collectors is the list of collectors of the specimen. Convert into the format of lastname, firstname initials e.g. Stark, Athony T. or Banner, B. Put periods between and at the end of any initials, and if there are multiple collectors separate them with a semi-colon character
- Other collectors - Do not fill in this field
- Field number is the collector's unique field book ID, usually a series of letters and numbers that are found close to the collector's name
- Determination - Find the taxanomic name of the specimen, using the international plant names index (IPNI) as a guide. Split the name into the relevant ranks of family, genus, species, subspecies, variety, and form. Do not populate any of these ranked fields with guesses if the information does not exist as part of the data input
- Start date is the start date of the collection. Format it to be DD/MM/YYYY
- End date is the end date of the collection. Format it to be DD/MM/YYYY
- Locality name is the location where the specimen was collected. Look for details of place names that might include distances to nearby towns. Split out any details of country or states into the separate country and state fields.
- The geocoordinate latitude and longitude values split into the separate latitude and longitude fields. Keep the formatting of degrees, minutes, seconds or decimal degrees. Infer the coordinate precision based on the data and enter a numeric value in the coord precision field. If geocoords are supplied as degrees, enter Coord. Precision as either 1 (for Deg) | 0.0166667 (for Min) | 0.0002778 (for Sec). If geocoords are supplied as decimal, enter Coord. Precision as number of decimal places. eg. for -21.17740, 143.91260 enter 0.00001, for -21.17, 143.91 enter 0.01. Use the picklist values for the verb. coord system field and populate that field based on the verbatim geocoordinate details.
- Any specific details mentioned about the surrounding area of the collection of the specimen should be placed in the habitat field
- Det Determiners is the list of determiners of the specimen. Convert into the format of lastname, firstname initials e.g. Stark, Athony T. or Banner, B. Put periods between and at the end of any initials, and if there are multiple collectors separate them with a semi-colon character. If there are no determiner names but a journal reference then put that journal reference in the Det. Reference field. Populate the Det. Source field with cit. if there is a journal reference or field if there is a determiner name.
- Look for mention of elevation or altitude, and populate the (Min) elevation field with the numerical part of that data, and the Max Elevation as well if a range has been provided, and the elevation units field with the unit reference, typically ft or m
- Any other text sentences should be placed in the Unit Notes field
- From the image attempt to fill in the Phenology group of fields with a y if that trait is present and leave it blank otherwise, except for the Fertile/Sterile field which should have an f for fertile or s for sterile
